data.title: Full-Disk Encryption Not Enforced
data.summary: Portable devices did not have full-disk encryption enforced, so a lost or stolen machine discloses its contents to anyone who removes the drive or boots from external media.
data.description:
Without full-disk encryption, operating system account passwords protect nothing: the drive can be removed and read, or the machine booted from external media, and every file is available.

That includes more than documents — cached credentials, browser profiles with saved passwords and session cookies, SSH and cloud keys, and locally synchronised copies of corporate data. A stolen laptop therefore becomes a route into the network rather than only a data-loss event.

Partial deployment is the usual state: encryption applied to new builds but not older devices, or enabled without the keys being escrowed, which leads to it being disabled when someone is locked out.
data.recommendation:
* Enforce full-disk encryption on all portable devices through device management, and report on compliance.
* Escrow recovery keys centrally so recovery never requires disabling encryption.
* Require pre-boot authentication, and configure firmware passwords with boot from external media disabled.
* Enable remote wipe, and define a reporting path for lost devices that is faster than the working day.
data.short_recommendation: Enforce full-disk encryption with centrally escrowed keys.
